A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe the same LeapAlign work and include Appendices A–I. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original Flux fine-tuning experiments in Section 6, SD3.5-M experiments in Appendix B, component ablations, and qualitative generation results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative results in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same two-step leap construction, latent connectors, gradient discounting, reward objective, and trajectory-similarity weighting.

E1.justification: Both versions use HPDv2, MJHQ-30k, and GenEval for the same general preference and compositional alignment tasks. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains DanceGRPO, MixGRPO, ReFL, DRaFT-LV, and DRTune as comparators. Tables 3–4 retain their same direct-gradient comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 retains the same data splits, sample counts, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and sampling settings. Appendix B also retains the SD3.5-M setting of 512 × 512 resolution and 200 training iterations.

E4.justification: The six component analyses in Figure 4, training curves in Appendix A, nested-gradient and loss-threshold analyses in Appendix C, and qualitative comparisons are unchanged.

E5.justification: The score tables and training curves retain the same statistical reporting. No run-count or seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains LeapAlign's HPSv2.1 score of 0.4092 and GenEval overall score of 0.7420; Appendix B's Table 4 retains its SD3.5-M HPSv2.1 score of 0.3915.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Sections 3–4 and the derivations of one-step leap prediction and backpropagated gradients in Appendices F–G are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about efficient early-step updates, preserved gradient information, stable fine-tuning, and improved image quality and alignment.

C2.justification: Section 5 retains the differentiable-reward requirement and discussion of applicability to few-step models. Interpretations concerning early-step updates, nested gradients, reward evaluation, and generalization in Section 6 and the appendices are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendix E retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, GPU count, training schedules, and baseline reproduction instructions. The project-page and baseline-checkpoint links are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the comparisons with prior methods, and all 66 references are unchanged. Adding a person to the acknowledgements does not revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 relocates and expands the author email list and updates the dates. Section 8 adds Kaiwen Zheng to the acknowledgements and removes the ARC Future Fellowship funding sentence. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised contact-information placement changes the front-page abstract box and slightly reflows pages 1–3, including the position of Table 1. Figures and tables retain their content and design; every appendix page renders identically.

improvement.justification: v3 retains the same method, empirical evidence, derivations, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information, including all appendices. The contact-information updates, acknowledgement edits, funding-sentence removal, and small layout shifts do not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
